How to fix it

Round the 0.5 mm fillet to a 3 mm radius
Stress piles up in the 0.5 mm fillet. A fillet of 3 mm (about half the 6 mm wall) spreads it out. With that radius the peak is usually about 1.4x the 15.2 MPa beam stress, roughly 21.3 MPa (safety factor 2.35).
re-run: peak 24.5 MPa, safety factor 2.04, marginal
Thicken the wall at the peak from 6 to 9.75 mm
The wall through the peak is 6 mm. To reach safety factor 2.5 it needs 9.75 mm (+62%), because bending stress falls with thickness squared.
re-run: peak 21.5 MPa, safety factor 2.32, marginal
Add a triangular gusset across the inside corner
The peak sits where two walls meet and bend. A gusset as thick as the wall, with legs about half as long as the shorter wall, ties them together and usually cuts the corner stress by half or more.
re-run: peak 10.3 MPa, safety factor 4.84, holds
Shorten the lever arm from 58.8 to 22.3 mm
The load acts 58.8 mm from the critical section. Moving a support or the load to within 22.3 mm brings the bending stress to the target.

fixturewall x=min
part2 holes, 1 inside fillets, 0 sharp inside corners, walls about 6 mm

Assumptions

  1. Linear elastic material and small deflections (no yielding redistribution, no buckling).
  2. PLA (3D printed): E 3500 MPa, Poisson 0.36, max principal vs tensile strength 50 MPa (Prusament PLA technical data sheet; Ultimaker PLA TDS).
  3. Loads are static and applied all at once; no impact, vibration or fatigue.
  4. Printed part treated as isotropic at 100% infill; across the layers it is roughly 60% as strong. Pass --print-direction to check that.
  5. Brittle failure: judged by the largest tensile principal stress.
  6. Bolted holes are rigidly held over the hole and a washer sized ring (twice the hole radius).
  7. Wall supports push but cannot pull (frictionless contact, solved iteratively).
  8. Contact between separate parts, friction and preload are not modeled.

Notes

  • Built from bracket.py with thickness=6, width=25, height=80, depth=90, fillet=0.5, hole=4.5.
Made with Wobbl 0.1.0. Solver CalculiX 2.23. Total time 95 s.
